findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. This is the strongest part of the page.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: A link to the next steps sits near the top, so a newcomer who only wants to try Athena can skip the long study.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself.

findings.text: The second section on the page shows a failure message instead of evidence. The page promises that Athena records models, verdicts and costs, so a newcomer meets a missing demo exactly where proof was expected.
findings.source: Check it on a real job — "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: The page lives at Athena's address, but the title is about another project, firstmate, which a newcomer has not heard of. They have to read three paragraphs before it is clear that the page is a sample of Athena's output.
An owner-only link sits in the introduction. A newcomer is not the owner, so the link is confusing and adds noise.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: Most of the page is a detailed state machine of firstmate's internals: exit codes, pending-close records, places-held. It shows that every statement is traced to a claim, but a newcomer deciding whether to try Athena has to scroll past a lot of it.
findings.source: Transitions; Counters; Claims and sources (45 claims)

findings.text: Several glossary entries define a term by saying the source does not define it (in scope, captain call, durable record, endpoint, heartbeat, wake). This is honest, but it leaves the reader without working definitions.
findings.source: in scope — "The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it."

findings.text: The next steps are concrete: prerequisites, the clone command, the setup script and a one-line first command. A newcomer knows exactly what to do next.
findings.source: Next steps — "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The page does not say what a run costs or which model accounts are needed beyond Claude Code. A newcomer cannot judge the risk before pressing Enter.
findings.source: Next steps — "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask \"add a changelog\". ... press Enter to run it on your repository."
